quotes.text: I don't think it would have changed the Fed, because if you look at the economy in general seems to be doing very well right now.
I think the Fed was on course to raise rates in December, probably not 50 basis points as we were talking about last week, but at least 25.
And now that Jensen came back and the market is rallied and, you know, my take is that we really look at Nvidia as being the Federal Reserve of AI.
Because they've been financing so much of the build out that that might continue or at least not recede as hard as we were figuring it was going to receive last week.
That that 50% of GDP will continue and that, yeah, the Fed's on course to raise rates and the last thing I'll say is they should raise rates.
I think it's the appropriate thing for the Fed to do. There is a thing called too low an interest rate that can be a problem.
I don't think we're quite there yet, but we're certainly not at restrictive levels.
I think right here, you're right, that range of around 5% plus or minus 25 basis points is where it should be.
It gets messy either way if, if we see serious signs that the economy is slowing, then I think rates will go down a lot.
Or if we see serious signs that we're getting an inflation spurt and then rates would go up.
Now, if I had to guess, I think the bigger risk is the economy slows rather than heats up.
I mean, they're neither one of them is zero, and that's why I'm kind of constructive in the bond market if I can buy bonds at around 5% return or 5% yield.

We've been having a conversation with our clients for the last month or so. Our quant systems pivot us to a risk-off macro regime which is a signal to our clients across the global byside to take down their growth and tighten their net exposure.

There's three wealth taxes on the ballot, California, Colorado, Washington.
If those wealth tax votes go in a way that's obviously not favorable for Wall Street, you're going to have two catalysts that are negative.
One catalyst is you're going to force billionaires to actually, you know, sell assets and and and raise cash that's negative for the market on the near-term basis.

But from a longer-term basis in our opinion, we think that will be a signal for 2028 and you're going to get a signal that candidates will start to campaign on significant redistributed policies which will challenge the free cash flow assumptions that hockey stick back to positive in 2028, 2029, and
Our macro weather model currently views the positioning cycle as a meaningful headwind for asset markets.
Well, respectfully we would have said to sell in September when our systems triggered risk-off.
In our opinion, if you're if you're fully invested here, you need to at the bare minimum downshift your beta, rotate into things that are less high beta, less cyclical, up in quality.
